wiki_text: In January 2026 the Trung Nam-Sideros River consortium won Vietnam's first international competitive tender for an LNG power project under PDP8, and on April 10, 2026 signed the investment-business contract with the Khanh Hoa People's Committee for the VND57.4 trillion (US$2.18 billion) Ca Na LNG project: a 1,500 MW CCGT plant plus an LNG import terminal with a regasification throughput of 1-1.2 million tonnes per year, a 220,000 m3 storage tank, an import berth and a 2,400 m breakwater, on about 140 ha of land and water in the former Thuan Nam district (Ninh Thuan, now part of Khanh Hoa). Commercial operation is required before December 31, 2030.

In April 2026, Nebula Energy's AG&P LNG agreed to acquire the remaining 51% of the Cai Mep LNG terminal from developer Hai Linh Co Ltd, taking it to 100% ownership (it bought 49% in March 2024); the deal remains subject to regulatory approvals and closing conditions. AG&P describes the 3 mtpa terminal as mechanically completed, commissioned and ramped up over the preceding 12 months, with 220,000 m3 of storage across three tanks, breakbulk reloading capability, 14 truck-loading bays, and potential to double capacity.

The Son My LNG Terminal is developed by Son My LNG Terminal LLC, a joint venture in which PV GAS holds 61% and AES 39% of charter capital. Per the July 2023 investment policy approval, Phase 1 is designed for 3.6 mtpa, expanding to 6 mtpa total through the terminal in Phase 2 (2027-2030), with potential long-run expansion to 10 mtpa. The signed joint venture agreement was exchanged in August 2025; latest planned start is Q1 2027 and construction had not begun as of mid-2026.
